prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Context: Meridian region dense terminal airspace (hub, domestic, cargo/GA aerodromes), near capacity. Airports: Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport (keep local safety/command authority). System-of-interest: Regional Flow Platform (alias Cedarbell), shared ATFM/A-CDM coordination layer; doesn't replace ATC, airport control rooms, airline operational control centers, ground handling dispatch. Parts: Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, Slot Allocation Engine, Airport CDM Portal, Digital Briefing Room, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, Contingency Operations Console, Weather Ingest Gateway, Flight Data Exchange, Surface Surveillance Adapter, Airline Interface Adapter, Alert Distribution Hub, Performance Analytics Warehouse, Audit Event Ledger, Identity Access Service, Business Rules Registry, Time Synchronization Service, Collaborative Decision Log, North/South Runway Meter, East/West Apron Sensor, Sector Load Monitor, Gate Conflict Detector, Common Situation Display. External: airline reservation, crew, baggage, commercial, national surveillance, avionics (identity, authorized data in, approved info out, audit). Actors: Regional Flow Manager (primary), Airline Operations Coordinator, Network Operations Liaison, Aircraft Operator Representative, Slot Coordinator, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Airport Duty Manager, Ground Handling Dispatcher, Deicing Coordinator, Meteorology Briefing Officer, Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator, Data Governance Steward, System Support Engineer. Shared picture items: Flight Intent Message, Airport Capacity Plan, Target Off Block Time, Calculated Takeoff Time, Airport Acceptance Rate, Tactical Regulation Proposal, Collaborative Decision Log entries, Post Operations Report. Modes: Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State (must support rapid...), Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, Slot Compliance State. Requirements: stakeholders must assign accountable representatives, keep contacts current, follow data use rules, support post-operational review. Daily cycle: morning pre-tactical baseline before bank lock, owned by Regional Flow Manager (horizon, cutover, checkpoints). Flows: platform builds demand from schedules, seasonal allocations, overnight changes, Flight Intent Message; Flight Data Exchange normalizes into single reference record; Demand Prediction Service outputs demand by time band/runway direction/terminal area/flow; Airline Operations Coordinator reviews intent deviations; Aircraft Operator Representative validates priorities per Business Rules Registry; Meteorology Briefing Officer weather outlook -> Weather Ingest Gateway -> Capacity Assessment Module (forecast issue time

New part:
S059: The Military Airspace Liaison confirms whether shared airspace assumptions remain valid for the morning and identifies any conditional availability that must be treated as uncertain.
S060: The Tower Supervisor sends the Runway Inspection Note before the first planning consolidation window.
S061: The Tower Supervisor also declares anticipated runway configuration, usable operating length assumptions, and any local sequencing constraints that affect the North Runway Meter and South Runway Meter.
S062: The Airport Duty Manager confirms terminal opening status, essential facility readiness, and airport service constraints that may affect the first operational waves.
S063: The Ramp Control Lead reviews early stand readiness using information from the Ramp Movement Board, East Apron Sensor, West Apron Sensor, and handling coordination calls.
S064: The Ground Handling Dispatcher confirms whether planned handling teams and equipment coverage are sufficient for the expected concentration of turns in each apron area.
S065: The Handling Resource Planner compares the demand curve with available ground resources and flags time bands where aircraft turn performance is likely to reduce stand availability.
S066: The Capacity Assessment Module combines the runway declaration, weather outlook, airspace constraints, stand readiness, and ground resource assumptions into a proposed Airport Acceptance Rate by period.
S067: The proposed Airport Acceptance Rate is tested against the demand profile to identify overloads, underused capacity, and points where a Ground Delay Program may become necessary.
S068: The Slot Coordinator uses the Slot Allocation Engine to prepare an initial slot feasibility view but does not publish binding Calculated Takeoff Time values during baseline construction.
S069: The Departure Metering Service estimates provisional Target Off Block Time sensitivity so planners can see how small changes in capacity would affect stand occupancy and departure queues.
S070: The Arrival Regulation Console highlights inbound demand periods where holding, speed control, or upstream sequencing may be needed if the forecast capacity materializes.
S071: The Digital Briefing Room displays the emerging Airport Capacity Plan and records unresolved assumptions in the Collaborative Decision Log for confirmation during the morning coordination briefing.
S072: The Common Situation Display presents the approved pre-tactical baseline as the shared reference for Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, and early Recovery Phase decisions.
S073: When the baseline is approved, the Alert Distribution Hub notifies participating roles that the morning plan is available and that changes must be entered through controlled Regional Flow Platform functions.
S074: The Performance Analytics Warehouse retains the baseline inputs, capacity declarations, and approval timestamps so the Post Operations Report can compare planned performance with actual outcomes.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
